writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic02w. Claims: every checkable statement in the stem, options and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers soul singers or the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, so c1, c2 and c4 need web evidence from the checkers. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for each distractor: Tina Turner was billed as the Queen of Rock and Roll, Diana Ross led the Supremes and Whitney Houston was nicknamed The Voice; none is known as the Queen of Soul. Argued against the key: the title has been Franklin's since the late 1960s, and no other singer holds it in common use. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Franklin and all three distractors are known worldwide, and the nickname travels with her records. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: None. c4 is a dated first (1987), not an open record.
